newsitem.title: JAPAN: Two Japan firms aim at merger in telecom reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Two Japan firms aim at merger in telecom reshuffle.

text.p: Two Japanese telecoms companies said on Wednesday that they were aiming to work out a merger pact by the end of the month, a move analysts said signalled the first step toward a major realignment of the industry here.

Haruo Murakami, vice president of long-distance carrier Japan Telecom Co Ltd, told a news conference that if an agreement was reached by the end of March, overseas carrier International Telecom Japan Inc (ITJ) would be merged with his firm around October.

Murakami also said he had hopes for further tie-ups in the future, including with Japan's top international carrier KDD (Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd), with electric power company affiliate TTNet, and with one of the world's three international telecom consortia.

KDD is already allied with WorldPartners, a loosely knit group led by U.S. telecoms giant AT&T. The other two global alliances are Concert, linking British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp of the United States, and Global One, which groups Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and America's Sprint Corp.

Analysts dubbed the restructuring signalled by the proposed merger inevitable, given Japan's moves to deregulate the sector, harsh global competition and the overwhelming dominance of domestic giant Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT), now poised to enter the international telecom field.
"It's the first sign of a significant reorganisation in the international market, which was inevitable," said Andrew Haskins, an analyst at HSBC James Capel Japan.

"The situation in the international market is that there are three (Japanese) operators, none of which is large enough on a global scale and which are facing a massive increase in competition from foreign operators and from domestic operators like NTT," Haskins said.
ITJ is one of Japan's smaller overseas carriers. The other two are former monopoly KDD and unlisted IDC Corp.
Japan Telecom, DDI Corp and Teleway Japan Corp are NTT's competitors in the domestic long-distance sector.

Under a plan worked out late last year, NTT is set to be restructured into a set of firms including one which can operate international services, under the wing of a holding company. Japan's legal barriers between international and domestic telecoms business will be dismantled from April.

NTT hopes to get its first taste of global business this year by offering special services to Japanese multinationals with offices around the world -- although those plans could hit a snag in the United States due to trade friction.

NTT and KDD on Wednesday confirmed a report that the United States had delayed approval for U.S. licences, a move Japanese media attributed to Washington's annoyance at Japan's retention of a 20 percent ceiling on foreign stakes in both companies.
Analysts, meanwhile, said that the product of a merger of Japan Telecom and ITJ would still be too small to compete successfully with NTT in the international field.

"Japan Telecom even together with ITJ is not going to be in a position to provide significant competition to the big new player about to enter the international market -- NTT," Haskins said. "If they merge with KDD and affiliates of the regional power companies, then that company might be in a position to be strong competition with NTT in the international market."
Whether DDI -- currently Japan's second largest phone operator -- would join in some new domestic grouping also remains unclear, analysts said.
DDI president Yusai Okuyama said on Tuesday that DDI was looking for links with domestic or foreign carriers, but that NTT appeared to be foreign carriers' preferred ally.
Analysts said, however, that NTT had no need to rush into the arms of any global group.

"NTT is the world's biggest and potentially the world's most powerful telecommunications company," Haskins said. "I think it may join one of the global alliances eventually...but I don't think they have a pressing need to do so right away."
